text:
incident-bot: ALERT > p99 latency spike detected for customer AtlasLogistics (dedicated pool: atlas-eu-west-1). threshold breached (p99 > 3.0s) · auto-page on-call
Maya (oncall): I’m on it — looking at the pool metrics now. Can someone pull the per-tenant QPS and KV cache hit rates?
Sam (runtime): grabbing traces. initial look: p95 ~ 1.2s -> 3.4s, p99 ~ 2.8s -> 6.1s over the last 7m.
Lee (platform): checking infra — no recent deploys to that pool. Node CPU/GPU utilization high on 3 of 6 instances.
Jordan (AM): FYI I’ve already pinged AtlasOps to let them know we’re investigating. They report slow order processing around the same time.
AtlasOps: we’re seeing order latency increase ~4–6s and some timeouts. Impacting ~8% of requests. We’re starting to queue orders at the app layer.
Maya (oncall): classification? P1 if customer-visible and impacts core workflow. Jordan, can you confirm severity?
Jordan (AM): Confirmed P1 for Atlas — revenue hitting customers during EU morning. Please prioritize.
Sam (runtime): quick triage: request distribution looks skewed to older model variant (v1-int8) on few nodes — KV cache miss rate spiked from 7% -> 42% for tenant prefix. Could be cache eviction storm after a GC.
Lee (platform): the autoscaler didn’t spin up new nodes because node boot times hit our quota throttle. I can temporarily increase reserved capacity for atlas pool. Need sign-off to force a warm-up replica set.
Maya (oncall): do it. Add two warm replicas and route 30% traffic to shared failover pool while we stabilize.
Lee (platform): invoking command: ```rwctl pool scale --pool atlas-eu-west-1 --add 2 --grace 60s```
Lee (platform): also creating route override: ```rwctl route override --customer atlas --region eu-west-1 --target shared-eu-west-backup --pct 30 --ttl 300```
Sam (runtime): disabling N-best reranking and stochastic sampling for this customer temporarily — reduce server-side compute. ```/api/configs/set atlas rerank=false sampling=0```
AtlasOps: we can accept fallback to shared pool for ~20% of traffic for the next hour. Please keep us updated.
Maya (oncall): running tenant isolation checks now — verifying noisy neighbor.
Sam (runtime): isolation check: tenant CPU per-request is normal; the spike correlates to a short-lived batch of long-context requests (seq len 2048) from one internal job. Not a multi-tenant attack.
Maya (oncall): can we throttle long-context requests for atlas tenant temporarily?
Sam (runtime): yes — applying per-tenant soft limit: ```/api/limits/set atlas max_seq_len=1024 window=10m``` — applying now.
Lee (platform): warm replicas are up (+2). routing override applied. Node utilization dropping on the problematic hosts.
incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE > p95=1.1s p99=2.9s (was p99=6.1s) after mitigations (10m window).
Jordan (AM): telling AtlasOps the mitigations and ETA for full recovery ~20–30m. They asked for a short blurb to send to their customers — drafting.
AtlasOps: thanks — sending note now. Keep logs for postmortem.
Maya (oncall): next steps: 1) keep overrides for 30m, 2) monitor KV cache warmup, 3) validate no error rate regressions, 4) prepare rollback of route if stable. Assigning to Sam for runtime follow-up and to Lee for capacity follow-up.
Sam (runtime): I’ll continue running trace sampling and will onboard a specific eval prompt to monitor quality impact from rerank disable.
Lee (platform): I’ll raise temporary reserved capacity with infra and follow-up with infra-changes PR to tune autoscale thresholds.
Maya (oncall): handoff in 25m to next oncall (Chris). Chris please join thread at 19:30 UTC for handoff.
incident-bot: PAGE > @Chris (next-oncall) scheduled handoff in 25m.
Sam (runtime): observed a small increase in 500s during rerank toggle (0.2% -> 0.5%) — rolling back rerank to 10% sample to balance quality.
Maya (oncall): any customer-visible regressions after that change?
AtlasOps: minor flakiness on rare prompts, but orders are flowing. 98.5% success rate now.
Jordan (AM): capture timeline and impacts. We’ll prepare an executive summary for Atlas and internal incident report.
Maya (oncall): tagging for postmortem: root cause suspected = cache eviction + long-context burst + autoscaler throttle. Postmortem owners: Sam (runtime), Lee (platform), Jordan (customer comms).
incident-bot: INCIDENT > STATUS=stabilized · assigned=Sam,Lee,Jordan · severity=P1 · next-update=10m
Maya (oncall): good work team. Keep monitoring for 1h then start recovery playbook.
Sam (runtime): will follow up with traces + suggested mitigations: per-tenant queueing, pre-warm policy for scheduled jobs, and stricter long-context throttles.
Lee (platform): filing infra ticket to add conservative headroom on reserved capacity for high-tier customers.
Jordan (AM): sending final customer update now. Will attach live metrics.
AtlasOps: we appreciate the fast response. Please include the temporary route override and limit changes in the postmortem.
Maya (oncall): recorded. Closing war-room for now — re-open if p99 creeps >3s again. Postmortem required. :white_check_mark:
